Sql.FindAccount:
-- Account holder plus everyone sharing the same phone number.
-- Parameters: @mobile, @type
-- Returns: name, password_hash, patient_id (one row per linked patient)
SELECT m.NOM AS name,
       CAST(NULL AS varchar(200)) AS password_hash,   -- TODO: no password column exists yet
       p.ADMI AS patient_id
FROM [DPERSONEL].dbo.PERSONEL p
OUTER APPLY (SELECT TOP 1 NOM FROM [DATA1].dbo.MALADE WHERE ADMIP = p.ADMI ORDER BY DATEIN DESC) m
WHERE LTRIM(RTRIM(p.TEL)) = @mobile
   OR LTRIM(RTRIM(ISNULL(p.TEL1, ''))) = @mobile
Sql.GetRequests:
-- Lab visits: the 3rd character of ADMI is the department, L = Lab.
-- Parameters: @mobile
SELECT m.ADMI AS request_nb,
       CONVERT(varchar(19), m.DATEIN, 120) AS order_datetime,
       'V' AS status,                                 -- TODO: real status column unknown
       CAST(NULL AS varchar(400)) AS pdf_path,        -- TODO: PDFs live on client PCs, see spec 7.4
       CAST(NULL AS varchar(19)) AS report_datetime,  -- TODO: release time unknown
       LTRIM(RTRIM(m.NOM)) AS patient_name
FROM [DATA1].dbo.MALADE m
JOIN [DPERSONEL].dbo.PERSONEL p ON p.ADMI = m.ADMIP
WHERE (LTRIM(RTRIM(p.TEL)) = @mobile OR LTRIM(RTRIM(ISNULL(p.TEL1, ''))) = @mobile)
  AND SUBSTRING(m.ADMI, 3, 1) = 'L'
ORDER BY m.DATEIN
Sql.GetResults:
-- Lab results for one order. -- Parameters: @mobile, @requestnb -- @mobile is not optional: without it any patient could read any report by guessing a visit number. -- RETAT = 1 is the released state. SELECT LTRIM(RTRIM(v.NOM)) AS name, CONVERT(varchar(10), p.NAISSANCE, 23) AS birthdate, r.SERIAL AS id, COALESCE(NULLIF(LTRIM(RTRIM(d.DESCRIP)), ''), LTRIM(RTRIM(r.DESCRIP))) AS test_name, 'N' AS is_title, CAST(NULL AS varchar(50)) AS group_name, '' AS group_instruction, '' AS group_clinical_remark, NULLIF(LTRIM(RTRIM(d.UNITE)), '') AS unit, -- Reference range from DATAPRIX.dbo.NLAB1, picked for this patient's sex and age. -- Wrapped in a div to match the MedVault capture ("
13.4-17.6
"). CASE WHEN NULLIF(LTRIM(RTRIM(ISNULL(rr.VALUEL, ''))), '') IS NOT NULL AND NULLIF(LTRIM(RTRIM(ISNULL(rr.VALUEH, ''))), '') IS NOT NULL THEN '
' + LTRIM(RTRIM(rr.VALUEL)) + '-' + LTRIM(RTRIM(rr.VALUEH)) + '
' WHEN NULLIF(LTRIM(RTRIM(ISNULL(rr.VALUEH, ''))), '') IS NOT NULL THEN '
< ' + LTRIM(RTRIM(rr.VALUEH)) + '
' WHEN NULLIF(LTRIM(RTRIM(ISNULL(rr.VALUEL, ''))), '') IS NOT NULL THEN '
> ' + LTRIM(RTRIM(rr.VALUEL)) + '
' ELSE NULL END AS ref_range, CAST(NULL AS varchar(1)) AS test_type, TRY_CAST(r.CODE AS int) AS test_id, 'Y' AS is_valid, TRY_CAST(COALESCE(NULLIF(LTRIM(RTRIM(r.CNOMLAB)), ''), d.LAB) AS int) AS category_num, CASE WHEN r.CARACT = 'L' THEN '' ELSE ISNULL(LTRIM(RTRIM(r.RESULT)), '') END AS result, CASE WHEN r.CARACT = 'L' THEN ISNULL(LTRIM(RTRIM(r.RESULT)), '') ELSE '' END AS result_txt, -- Display flag. Only set when the comparison is actually possible. CASE WHEN r.CARACT = 'L' OR TRY_CAST(LTRIM(RTRIM(r.RESULT)) AS float) IS NULL THEN '' WHEN TRY_CAST(rr.VALUEL AS float) IS NOT NULL AND TRY_CAST(LTRIM(RTRIM(r.RESULT)) AS float) < TRY_CAST(rr.VALUEL AS float) THEN 'Low' WHEN TRY_CAST(rr.VALUEH AS float) IS NOT NULL AND TRY_CAST(LTRIM(RTRIM(r.RESULT)) AS float) > TRY_CAST(rr.VALUEH AS float) THEN 'High' ELSE '' END AS sign, COALESCE(TRY_CAST(d.RANGER AS int), r.RANG) AS position, 'N' AS is_main, CAST(NULL AS varchar(20)) AS prev_result_val, '' AS prev_order_id, LTRIM(RTRIM(r.CODE)) AS field_num, ISNULL(LTRIM(RTRIM(r.REMARK)), '') AS clinical_remark, '' AS method_instruction, ISNULL(LTRIM(RTRIM(r.REMARK3)), '') AS code_remark, 'N' AS is_printed, CAST(NULL AS varchar(20)) AS calc_result, CAST(NULL AS varchar(20)) AS calc_unit, CAST(NULL AS varchar(1)) AS group_printed, 'N' AS need_validation, 'N' AS highlight_txt, COALESCE(TRY_CAST(d.RANGER AS int), r.RANG) AS group_order, 0 AS group_num, TRY_CAST(COALESCE(NULLIF(LTRIM(RTRIM(r.CNOMLAB)), ''), d.LAB) AS int) AS cat_num, LTRIM(RTRIM(n.DESCRIP)) AS cat_name, -- H / L / N, or NULL when no range applies or the result is not numeric. Never a literal 'N': -- ReferenceRanges.Annotate only computes a status when this arrives empty. CASE WHEN r.CARACT = 'L' OR TRY_CAST(LTRIM(RTRIM(r.RESULT)) AS float) IS NULL THEN NULL WHEN TRY_CAST(rr.VALUEL AS float) IS NOT NULL AND TRY_CAST(LTRIM(RTRIM(r.RESULT)) AS float) < TRY_CAST(rr.VALUEL AS float) THEN 'L' WHEN TRY_CAST(rr.VALUEH AS float) IS NOT NULL AND TRY_CAST(LTRIM(RTRIM(r.RESULT)) AS float) > TRY_CAST(rr.VALUEH AS float) THEN 'H' WHEN TRY_CAST(rr.VALUEL AS float) IS NOT NULL OR TRY_CAST(rr.VALUEH AS float) IS NOT NULL THEN 'N' ELSE NULL END AS result_status, CAST(NULL AS int) AS dec_pts FROM [DATA1].dbo.TRLAB r LEFT JOIN [DATAPRIX].dbo.RLAB1 d ON d.CODE COLLATE DATABASE_DEFAULT = r.CODE COLLATE DATABASE_DEFAULT LEFT JOIN [DATAPRIX].dbo.NOMLAB n ON n.CODE COLLATE DATABASE_DEFAULT = COALESCE(NULLIF(LTRIM(RTRIM(r.CNOMLAB)), ''), d.LAB) COLLATE DATABASE_DEFAULT JOIN [DATA1].dbo.MALADE v ON v.ADMI COLLATE DATABASE_DEFAULT = r.ADMI COLLATE DATABASE_DEFAULT JOIN [DPERSONEL].dbo.PERSONEL p ON p.ADMI COLLATE DATABASE_DEFAULT = v.ADMIP COLLATE DATABASE_DEFAULT -- One range row per test, chosen for this patient. '(' and blank mean "any sex" in this schema. -- Exact sex match wins over "any"; the narrowest matching age band wins after that. OUTER APPLY (SELECT TOP 1 nr.VALUEL, nr.VALUEH FROM [DATAPRIX].dbo.NLAB1 nr WHERE nr.CODE COLLATE DATABASE_DEFAULT = r.CODE COLLATE DATABASE_DEFAULT AND (LTRIM(RTRIM(ISNULL(nr.SEXE, ''))) = LTRIM(RTRIM(ISNULL(p.SEX, ''))) OR LTRIM(RTRIM(ISNULL(nr.SEXE, ''))) IN ('', '(')) AND (p.NAISSANCE IS NULL OR DATEDIFF(YEAR, p.NAISSANCE, v.DATEIN) BETWEEN nr.AGEL AND nr.AGEH) AND (NULLIF(LTRIM(RTRIM(ISNULL(nr.VALUEL, ''))), '') IS NOT NULL OR NULLIF(LTRIM(RTRIM(ISNULL(nr.VALUEH, ''))), '') IS NOT NULL) ORDER BY CASE WHEN LTRIM(RTRIM(ISNULL(nr.SEXE, ''))) = LTRIM(RTRIM(ISNULL(p.SEX, ''))) THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, (nr.AGEH - nr.AGEL), nr.LIGNE) rr WHERE r.ADMI COLLATE DATABASE_DEFAULT = @requestnb AND (LTRIM(RTRIM(p.TEL)) = @mobile OR LTRIM(RTRIM(ISNULL(p.TEL1, ''))) = @mobile) AND r.RETAT = 1 ORDER BY COALESCE(TRY_CAST(d.RANGER AS int), r.RANG), r.LIGNE
Sql.GetRadiologyStudies:
-- Imaging visits: 3rd character of ADMI, X = Radiology.
-- Parameters: @mobile
SELECT m.ADMI AS study_nb,
       CONVERT(varchar(19), m.DATEIN, 120) AS order_datetime,
       'V' AS status,
       CAST(NULL AS varchar(8)) AS modality,          -- TODO: modality not stored in MALADE
       CAST(NULL AS varchar(200)) AS study_name,      -- TODO
       CAST(NULL AS varchar(400)) AS pdf_path,        -- TODO: see spec 7.4
       CAST(NULL AS varchar(19)) AS report_datetime,
       LTRIM(RTRIM(m.NOM)) AS patient_name
FROM [DATA1].dbo.MALADE m
JOIN [DPERSONEL].dbo.PERSONEL p ON p.ADMI = m.ADMIP
WHERE (LTRIM(RTRIM(p.TEL)) = @mobile OR LTRIM(RTRIM(ISNULL(p.TEL1, ''))) = @mobile)
  AND SUBSTRING(m.ADMI, 3, 1) = 'X'
ORDER BY m.DATEIN

Sql.//Categories: OPEN: TRLAB.CNOMLAB holds the category as a code (01, 02, 07...). No lookup table exists in DATA1, so cat_name currently returns the code. Ask the lab for the names and map them in the CASE below.
Sql.//AbnormalFlag: TRLAB.ABNORMAL is NULL in all 242,297 rows, so sign is always ''. The app's High/Low highlighting will show nothing. Confirmed against the live database 2026-08-25.
Sql.//UnitsAndRanges:
CORRECTED 2026-09-09. The earlier note claiming ranges exist nowhere was wrong - it was written before DATAPRIX was available. Reference ranges live in DATAPRIX.dbo.NLAB1 (1942 rows, 900 test codes): VALUEL/VALUEH are the bounds, SEXE is M/F or "(" meaning any, AGEL/AGEH bound the age band. GetResults picks one row per test for the patient sex and age, formats it as
low-high
to match the MedVault capture, and computes result_status H/L/N plus sign High/Low from it. Units, test names, categories and ordering come from RLAB1 + NOMLAB.
Sql.//Databases: The read-only HIS account needs SELECT on three databases: DATA1 (visits and results), DPERSONEL (phone numbers) and DATAPRIX (test catalogue).
Sql.//ResultStatus: result_status MUST be selected as NULL, never as a literal N. ReferenceRanges.Annotate only computes High/Low when the value arrives empty, so a hardcoded N makes every result display as normal - including genuinely high ones - once ranges exist.
